text:
Eve W: Heads-up: we saw a small spike of KMS decrypt failures for restores from the cold-archive bucket across two regions. Not systemic but 5/200 restores returned AccessDenied in the last hour.
Oscar B: got a few alerts too. Error sample: "NotAuthorizedException: User arn:aws:iam::333222111:role/archive-restorer-new is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:333222111:key/kk-arch-09" (restore-job: r-9901).
Tegan: did we change any role naming or aliasing? We rolled a role rename and an alias migration for several service roles yesterday.
Eve W: yes we renamed archive-restorer -> archive-restorer-new and rotated a few key aliases in us-west-2 -> us-east-1 for DR alignment. I updated inline policies but did not touch CMK grants.
encops-bot: Alert: 5 decrypt failures for cmk kk-arch-09 between 2026-01-08T04:10:32Z and 2026-01-08T04:12:18Z. Trace excerpt: \n```
2026-01-08T04:11:03Z restore-worker ERROR job=r-9901 cause=AccessDenied kmsKey=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:333222111:key/kk-arch-09
CausedBy: NotAuthorizedException: Not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt for principal arn:aws:iam::333222111:role/archive-restorer-new
```
Oscar B: inventory shows existing grants on kk-arch-09 reference the old ARN arn:aws:iam::333222111:role/archive-restorer. Grants are immutable; they don't follow role renames. Also saw a couple grants with EncryptionContextSubset constraints referencing metadata keys that our S3 restore pipeline strips (x-amz-meta-snapshot-id vs snapshot_id) 5, which meant even when principal matched the EncryptionContextSubset didn't align.
Tegan: interesting 5 we have two issues then: orphaned grantee ARNs after rename, and mismatch in encryptionContext keys between when snapshots were uploaded and the current restore workflow.
Eve W: mitigation path: 1) create targeted CreateGrant calls for the new role preserving EncryptionContextSubset but using the exact key names that the restore pipeline supplies, 2) where cross-region copies exist, ensure the grantee principal includes the regional ARN shape, 3) for snapshots that used alternate encryption context keys, re-run a prep job to inject expected metadata into the restore job so constraints match.
infra-qa: quick checklist: list-grants -> map GrantId->GranteePrincipal->Constraints, cross-ref IAM to see which principals are missing, and then create scoped grants with retire_on timestamp. Also capture CloudTrail events.
encops-bot: Suggested commands (sanitized): \n```
aws kms list-grants --key-id kk-arch-09 --region us-east-1
aws kms create-grant --key-id kk-arch-09 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::333222111:role/archive-restorer-new --operations Decrypt --constraints EncryptionContextSubset={"snapshot_tag":"snap-202312-09"} --name temp-restore-snap-202312-09
```
Oscar B: I ran list-grants and found: \n- g-301 grantee arn:aws:iam::333222111:role/archive-restorer  Constraints:{"snapshot_id":"snap-202312-09"}
- g-302 grantee arn:aws:444555666:role/partner-copy  Constraints:{}
Note: partner-copy is cross-account and still valid.
Tegan: two delicate points: (A) when re-creating grants for the new role, preserve EncryptionContextSubset keys exactly as the pipeline will provide them (we had a mismatch snapshot_id vs snapshot_tag), and (B) use RetiringPrincipal or set retire-on window so we don't leave permanent grants lying around. Also log operator and ticket.
Eve W: I don't want to broad key-policy updates without sign-off; let's do targeted grants. Oscar, can you create temp grants for the five affected snapshot ids, set a 6-12 hour retire window, and attach grant ids to the incident?
Oscar B: running create-grant now with constraints matching the current restore headers. Example I used: \n```
aws kms create-grant --key-id kk-arch-09 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::333222111:role/archive-restorer-new --operations Decrypt --constraints EncryptionContextSubset={"snapshot_tag":"snap-202312-09"} --name tmp-restore-202312-09
```
Response: GrantId g-temp-901. CloudTrail CreateGrant event logged: ct-evt-112233.
Tegan: replays: do them in small batches and ensure the restore pipeline injects snapshot_tag header. If the pipeline can be fixed quickly to use the historic key name snapshot_id we should patch it to avoid future mismatches.
encops-bot: Audit suggestion: run nightly job that: 1) lists grants per CMK, 2) cross-references grantee principal ARNs against current IAM entities, 3) flags grants with missing principals and reports encryptionContext keys used. Pseudo-query: \n```
SELECT key_id, GrantId, GranteePrincipal, Constraints FROM kms_grants WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM iam_entities WHERE arn = GranteePrincipal)
```
Tegan: compliance note from sec-oncall: temporary grants are ok if scoped, retired promptly, and CloudTrail logs + incident ticket include user who created them. We'll retire g-temp-901 after replays. Also add a follow-up to adjust restore pipeline metadata keys.
Eve W: longer-term actions: 1) add KMS-grant sweep to RBAC rename runbook, 2) add preflight hook that fails renames if kms_grants reference the principals, 3) normalize restore metadata keys (snapshot_id vs snapshot_tag) and add backward-compatible header mapping during restore, 4) consider standardizing on key-policy statements for cross-account restores instead of many per-role grants.
infra-qa: replay results: 5 failing -> 0 after grants and header fix. I'll schedule a scan across all CMKs for orphaned grants and open a JIRA to normalize metadata.
encops-bot: Reminders: retire grants g-temp-901..g-temp-905 by calling retire-grant and attach retire CloudTrail events to INC-2026-417.
sec-oncall: filing INC-2026-417, approved mitigation. Keep monitoring for 24h. :white_check_mark:
